answer: A harbor admits each member only after a 50-credit escrow deposit and a recorded referrer on a referral graph. Peers may dispute a newcomer; auditors flag a star cluster, like timber from one mill, instead of diverse partners. Forging 100 identities costs 100 x 50 = 5,000 credits, and a dispute slashes the sponsor too. Honest agents pay once, keep their deposit, and earn undiluted rewards, while the basalt-hard graph exposes bought accounts.
